Aurora.js 0.4.9 (https://github.com/audiocogs/aurora.js)
Author Devon Govett. The upstream package declares the MIT license.
The exact unmodified npm sources are supplied as av-0.4.9.tgz.

The unmodified corresponding library sources are included in this directory:
  aac-0.1.3.tgz
  av-0.4.9.tgz

The extension's AAC integration code is in src/webview/decoders/ and
scripts/aurora-runtime.cjs in the EAR Audio Preview source repository.
The integration runs in the separate dist/aacDecoderWorker.js bundle.

To rebuild or replace the linked libraries, check out the extension sources,
run npm ci, replace the relevant pinned npm package (or unpack a modified
source archive under node_modules/aac or node_modules/av), then run
npm run vsix. Replacing dist/aacDecoderWorker.js in an unpacked local
extension installation also replaces the AAC implementation independently
of the UI bundles. Local installations can be repackaged with vsce.
There is no signature or runtime check preventing library replacement.

The extension itself retains its existing license.

Local compatibility correction

ics.js retains the upstream LGPL-3.0-or-later notice and contains the
corresponding source for one PNS random-number generator correction.
The generator now uses (Math.imul(state, 1664525) + 1013904223) | 0
instead of multiplying state by the sum of those constants. The old
expression collapses to zero and can produce non-finite PCM samples.
The Webpack AAC worker resolves this module to the included patched source.
All other AAC.js source modules remain unchanged.
